# Encrypted interoperability fixtures

The `*-encrypted-m{1,2}.rnc` fixtures encode `b"A" * 12288 + b"B" * 100`
with key `0x1234`, spanning two chunks. The `*-encrypted-mixed-m{1,2}.rnc`
fixtures encode the `INPUTS["mixed-"]` bytes in `test_interop.py`: several
different literal runs separated by repeated bytes. They exercise multiple key
rotations and method 2's single literals and bulk literal runs. Both methods
must retain the rotating key across the chunk boundary.

`upstream-encrypted-m{1,2}.rnc` were generated by the C implementation at
https://github.com/lab313ru/rnc_propack_source/blob/master/main.c and checked
with its own decoder. The source used on 2026-10-22 has SHA-256
`d1ad1c1b803d3218ce9f1d7cb5791b5cc508956d17d71f91317a797864fb4683`.

Compile that source with `cc -O2 main.c -o rnc`, write the raw bytes to `raw`,
and run these commands for each method (shown for method 1):

```sh
./rnc p raw upstream-encrypted-m1.rnc -m=1 -k=1234
./rnc u upstream-encrypted-m1.rnc decoded -k=1234
cmp raw decoded
```

`verified-encrypted-m{1,2}.rnc` were generated by Python `pack(raw, method=method,
key=0x1234)` after fixing key continuity and match-search termination. They were
independently decoded with the same C tool and compared byte-for-byte with `raw`.
These golden files test encoder compatibility without requiring a C compiler in
the test suite. If compression choices change, regenerate them only after
verifying the new output with an independent decoder.

The `-mixed-` variants were generated and verified using the same commands and
tool, substituting `INPUTS["mixed-"]` for the raw bytes and the matching filenames.
